hero.title: Dexterous robotic manipulation
hero.lead: From the material inside a fingertip to the policy coordinating several robots: we connect sensing, embodiment and learning for contact-rich manipulation.

introduction.title: Follow the contact, from sensor to skill.
introduction.text: Touch makes local geometry, force and interaction observable. Our projects ask how to design that observation, interpret it, and turn it into reliable action when objects, sensors or tasks change.
introduction.note: This collection includes MSEI work and earlier collaborative studies co-authored by Dandan Zhang. Each project links its original paper and identifies the hardware, evaluation setting and scope.

groups.title: Tactile sensors & materials
groups.description: Design the physical contact interface: optical structures, printable elastomers, multimodal sensing and computation inside the sensor.

projects.name: ViTacTip
projects.title: Design and Benchmarking of a Multimodality Sensor for Robotic Manipulation With GAN-Based Cross-Modality Interpretation
projects.question: How can one fingertip combine visual context with detailed contact sensing?
projects.approach: A transparent skin reveals the approaching object while internal biomimetic tips amplify deformation. Multi-task learning interprets hardness, material and texture; GAN models separate visual and tactile information.
projects.evidence: Benchmarks cover object recognition, contact localisation, pose regression and grating identification, alongside multimodal material recognition.
projects.scope: Vision and touch share one optical path. Proximity and force are derived perceptions; performance depends on calibration, objects and lighting in the reported tests.

projects.name: MagicTac
projects.title: MagicTac: A Novel High-Resolution 3D Multi-layer Grid-Based Tactile Sensor
projects.question: How can an internal three-dimensional grid make contact easier to observe?
projects.approach: A multi-layer grid embedded in a soft, printed body changes its appearance under normal motion, shear and rotation. Deformation fields and optical flow expose the contact pattern.
projects.evidence: The paper evaluates fine texture observation, dynamic contact, grating identification and contact localisation, together with fabrication time and cost.
projects.scope: Fabrication and performance measurements describe the reported design and printing conditions; they are not current purchasing estimates.

projects.name: CrystalTac
projects.title: CrystalTac: Vision-Based Tactile Sensor Family Fabricated via Rapid Monolithic Manufacturing
projects.question: Can a shared manufacturing process support different tactile sensing mechanisms?
projects.approach: Multi-material printing integrates components into a monolithic contact module. Five sensor branches combine illumination, marker displacement and visual information in different ways.
projects.evidence: Case studies examine object and texture recognition, see-through-skin sensing and customisation of internal structures, shapes and sizes.
projects.scope: This is a sensor family and fabrication study. The different designs expose different contact information and are not interchangeable without evaluation.

projects.name: i-Tac
projects.title: i-Tac: Inverse Design of 3D-Printed Tactile Elastomers with Tuneable Optical and Mechanical Properties
projects.question: Can desired optical and mechanical properties guide tactile material fabrication?
projects.approach: Multi-material PolyJet printing combines three resins. Mixture experiments and response-surface models map composition to transparency and hardness; multi-objective optimisation selects a feasible formulation.
projects.evidence: Experiments compare predicted and measured properties and fabricate sensor samples from both commercial and custom designs.
projects.scope: The feasible property range is specific to the characterised materials and printing process. A target must lie within that range.

projects.name: PixelTac
projects.title: A vision-based tactile sensor with in-sensor computing paradigm for seamless tactile sensing and perception
projects.question: What tactile processing can take place inside the sensor?
projects.approach: A computational pixel matrix and microcontroller integrate tactile acquisition with local processing. The pipeline progresses through pixel filtering, marker tracking, temporal-event extraction and force inference. PCA compresses marker trajectories before a quantised multilayer perceptron estimates three-axis contact force on the microcontroller.
projects.evidence: Pressing, squeezing and tapping experiments examine spatial deformation and temporal responses. Robot-controlled indentation against a force/torque sensor evaluates force inference, including ablations of feature dimension, calibration domain and network capacity. Supplementary videos show the sensing responses.
projects.scope: The model is trained offline and deployed for local inference. Accuracy depends on calibration and feature selection; the paper reports a trade-off between constrained in-sensor computation and force-estimation accuracy. These are sensor-perception experiments.

groups.title: Perception, data & learning
groups.description: Make contact information usable and testable through spatial representations, sensor evaluation, cross-sensor benchmarks and synthetic data.

projects.name: TacVerse
projects.title: TacVerse: A Multisensor Dataset and Benchmark for Cross-Sensor Vision-Based Tactile Perception
projects.question: How much does tactile perception change when the sensor changes?
projects.approach: A shared dataset contains 106,800 tactile images from seven optical sensor designs. It supports nine-class shape recognition, 30-class grating recognition and continuous force regression. Separate within-sensor, zero-shot transfer and few-shot adaptation protocols expose the effect of changing the sensing hardware.
projects.evidence: Cross-sensor heatmaps reveal large transfer gaps, while limited labelled target data improves force estimation without fully closing the gap. A representation study compares ResNet-18 and Vision Transformer initialisations, including masked-autoencoder pretraining using only training partitions.
projects.scope: The data come from controlled laboratory contacts. Grating and force transfer use fixed source sensors; this is not an exhaustive comparison of tactile foundation models or a closed-loop manipulation benchmark. Dataset files require Hugging Face sign-in and acceptance of access conditions.

projects.name: TacEva
projects.title: TacEva: A Performance Evaluation Framework for Vision-Based Tactile Sensors
projects.question: Which sensor is suitable for a particular contact task?
projects.approach: Task-relevant metrics and repeatable experimental pipelines compare intrinsic properties, standard sensing performance and robustness across tactile sensor designs.
projects.evidence: The framework evaluates sensors with different sensing mechanisms and reports performance by dimension, supporting informed selection and design refinement.
projects.scope: The comparison is tied to the tested hardware, calibration and protocols. Different metrics can favour different designs.

projects.name: SARL
projects.title: SARL: Spatially-Aware Self-Supervised Representation Learning for Visuo-Tactile Perception
projects.question: How can self-supervised features preserve the geometry needed for contact?
projects.approach: SARL extends BYOL with saliency alignment, patch-prototype distribution alignment and region-affinity matching on intermediate feature maps, alongside a global representation objective.
projects.evidence: Evaluation compares nine self-supervised baselines across six downstream tasks. The paper reports improved edge-pose estimation and stronger spatial representations.
projects.scope: The experiments evaluate fused visual–tactile perception. They do not establish a complete robot policy or universal cross-sensor transfer.

projects.name: MultiDiffSense
projects.title: MultiDiffSense: Diffusion-Based Multi-Modal Visuo-Tactile Image Generation Conditioned on Object Shape and Contact Pose
projects.question: Can controlled synthetic contact images reduce real data collection?
projects.approach: A shared diffusion model generates ViTac, TacTip and ViTacTip observations. CAD-derived depth maps and prompts describing sensor identity and contact pose condition the output.
projects.evidence: Tests use eight objects, including three novel objects, and unseen poses. A 50% real / 50% synthetic mixture retains competitive downstream pose-estimation performance in the reported study.
projects.scope: Synthetic images are model outputs. Their value is assessed through image comparisons and a downstream task, not visual realism alone.

projects.name: MagicGripper
projects.title: MagicGripper: A Mini-MagicTac Integrated Gripper Enabling Multimodal Perception in Contact-Rich Manipulation
projects.venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering 22, 24311–24332
projects.question: How can a gripper sense an object before and during contact?
projects.approach: Compact mini-MagicTac fingertips combine visual, proximity and tactile information. A printed multi-layer grid supplies contact features within a gripper-compatible form.
projects.evidence: Experiments study spatial resolution, contact localisation, force regression, manufacturing variation and robustness. Robot demonstrations cover teleoperated assembly, contact-based alignment and autonomous grasping.
projects.scope: The added task figures come from the earlier author manuscript. The main citation identifies the final journal article and its full author list.

projects.name: TacFR-Gripper
projects.title: TacFR-Gripper: A Reconfigurable Fin-Ray-Based Gripper with Tactile Skin for In-Hand Manipulation
projects.question: How can finger compliance and reconfiguration support in-hand manipulation?
projects.approach: A reconfigurable base carries Fin Ray-inspired compliant fingers with force-sensitive-resistor skin. Graph-based processing uses the spatial arrangement of tactile signals to support stable grasping.
projects.evidence: The work combines kinematic, workspace and load analysis with physical grasping, tactile-feedback and object-pose-control experiments.
projects.scope: The figure manuscript predates the journal article. Grasping and in-hand motion are evaluated on the reported object set and gripper configurations.

projects.name: TacPalm
projects.title: TacPalm: A Soft Gripper with a Biomimetic Optical Tactile Palm for Stable Precise Grasping
projects.question: Can a sensing palm improve grasp precision while the fingers stay soft?
projects.approach: A TacTip in the palm measures contact without embedding a camera in the flexible fingers. The grasping strategy combines light-contact detection, pose adjustment and loss-of-contact detection.
projects.evidence: On the reported artificial and household objects, the complete strategy achieves 97% grasp success and sub-millimetre placement precision.
projects.scope: The success rate concerns the paper’s test objects and staged grasping strategy; it is not a general performance guarantee for fragile-object handling.

projects.name: Tac-VGNN
projects.title: Tac-VGNN: A Voronoi Graph Neural Network for Pose-Based Tactile Servoing
projects.question: How can marker geometry become feedback for surface following?
projects.approach: A graph represents relationships between tactile markers. Voronoi-area features add contact-depth information to marker displacement, and a graph neural network estimates contact pose for servoing.
projects.evidence: The paper evaluates pose estimation, training efficiency and real surface-following tasks. Voronoi features improve depth estimation over the tested plain-GNN baseline.
projects.scope: The method is evaluated with TacTip marker observations and a specific pose-based servoing setup.

projects.name: ADM-DP
projects.title: ADM-DP: Adaptive Dynamic Modality Diffusion Policy through Vision-Tactile-Graph Fusion for Multi-Agent Manipulation
projects.question: Which sensory information matters at each stage of a coordinated task?
projects.approach: A diffusion policy combines RGB and point-cloud features, FSR tactile feedback and a graph of robot tool positions. Adaptive modality attention changes their relative contribution; each agent learns a policy while sharing spatial context.
projects.evidence: Seven simulated multi-agent tasks test coordinated manipulation, with modality ablations examining grasp refinement and inter-agent interference.
projects.scope: This study evaluates simulated tasks; real-robot deployment is identified as future work. Its tactile modality models FSR feedback, rather than optical tactile images.

projects.name: Bi-Touch
projects.title: Bi-Touch: Bimanual Tactile Manipulation with Sim-to-Real Deep Reinforcement Learning
projects.question: How can two arms coordinate manipulation using touch?
projects.approach: Two robot arms with TacTip sensors learn bimanual skills in Tactile Gym. Task rewards and a goal-update mechanism support reinforcement learning; tactile image translation bridges simulation and hardware.
projects.evidence: Physical trials test pushing, reorienting and gathering with previously unseen objects. The added figures show the object set, reorientation trajectories and responses to disturbances during gathering. Performance varies with object shape and perturbations; the triangular-prism reorientation case illustrates a failure mode.
projects.scope: Control uses tactile images and proprioception; external tracking markers provide evaluation measurements. A simulation-to-reality gap can cause excessive squeezing, and varied object geometry remains challenging. Simulation panels are labelled separately from hardware trials.

projects.name: TacMMs
projects.title: TacMMs: Tactile Mobile Manipulators for Warehouse Automation
projects.question: Can tactile feedback help mobile robots lift a shared load?
projects.approach: Each mobile robot carries a TacTip on a lifting platform. Contact estimates guide relative robot–object pose adjustment before cooperative lifting.
projects.evidence: In the two-robot study, tactile control achieves 66% average lifting success versus 34% for the tested visual-only approach, with larger gains for uneven mass distributions.
projects.scope: The experiments use two robots. Extension to larger teams is a proposed direction rather than a demonstrated result.

projects.name: One-shot robotic pouring
projects.title: One-Shot Domain-Adaptive Imitation Learning via Progressive Learning Applied to Robotic Pouring
projects.venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering 21(1), 541–554
projects.question: How can a learned skill adapt with one new demonstration?
projects.approach: A progressive imitation-learning framework first learns coarse visual concepts, then generates actions from sequential observations. An imaginary-learning phase uses CycleGAN image translation to create target-style training observations. One demonstration from a new scene supports adaptation of an already trained source policy.
projects.evidence: UR5 experiments vary the background, granular material and receiving container. The added sequences show physical executions before and after scene changes; comparisons in the manuscript evaluate coarse learning, fine action learning and domain adaptation separately.
projects.scope: One-shot refers to adaptation after source-domain training, not learning pouring from scratch. Generated observations are training data; the experimental sequences show physical execution. The study uses vision and granular materials rather than tactile feedback or liquid pouring.

approachFigure.title: From contact observations to adaptable manipulation
approachFigure.alt: Touch and vision provide observations of physical interaction. State representations and learned action policies support grasping and manipulation, with new contact observations informing subsequent action.
approachFigure.caption: Conceptual connection between sensing, representation, learned action and contact. These elements are investigated in different sensors, robots and tasks; the schematic does not describe one universal manipulation system.

resources.name: TacVerse
resources.description: Train and compare shape, grating and force-perception models across tactile sensors.
resources.requirements: Dataset access requires Hugging Face sign-in and acceptance of access conditions.

resources.name: MultiDiffSense
resources.description: Prepare geometry-conditioned data, generate tactile observations and evaluate image and pose-estimation performance.
resources.requirements: Read the model-weight, dataset and GPU requirements before training.

resources.name: ADM-DP
resources.description: Explore vision–tactile–graph fusion and adaptive diffusion policies for multi-agent manipulation.
resources.requirements: Training requires per-arm demonstrations and the simulator stack described in the reuse guide.

resources.name: Tac-VGNN
resources.description: Build Voronoi graph representations from tactile markers and estimate pose for tactile servoing.
resources.requirements: Real servoing depends on calibrated tactile hardware and robot control.

resources.name: Bi-Touch
resources.description: Study the author-released bimanual Tactile Gym branch and the associated physical task demonstrations.
resources.requirements: The original author branch is linked because the task-specific release is hosted there.

resources.name: TacEva
resources.description: Explore tactile sensor evaluation methods and the project’s comparison protocols.
resources.requirements: Use the metric definitions and calibration procedure when comparing sensor designs.

outlook.title: When should the sensor change?
outlook.text: Connect material and geometric design choices to the observations a manipulation task actually needs.

outlook.title: What transfers across hardware?
outlook.text: Separate changes in contact physics from changes in image appearance, and measure how much new data adaptation requires.

outlook.title: How should contact guide action?
outlook.text: Use uncertainty and changing sensory relevance to decide when to refine a grasp, gather more evidence or coordinate another robot.

provenanceNote: Project descriptions summarise the linked primary papers. Figures are original paper or author-project material, with source links and credits.
